text:
Anya M.: Heads-up: during a quantization eval run last night some artifacts in S3 contained raw prompt metadata (customer_id + example_id). Not a prod breach but definitely PII exposure risk. Threading here to triage. Details: eval-runner v2.3.1 wrote artifacts to s3://redwood-eval-artifacts/staging/2026-03-18/<run-id>/ with metadata.json per sample.

Matt R.: Ack. Which step wrote the metadata? runner or harness?

Diego V.: Looks like the runner's artifact writer serializes the entire request object. There's a helper `write_artifact(obj)` that just `json.dump(request)` — so it pulls through provenance fields. Repro: checkout branch `quant-2026` and run `python -m eval.runner --ci --dry-run` then inspect `artifacts/`.

Anya M.: Immediate mitigation plan: 1) deny public read on the S3 prefix (already done?), 2) rotate CI read keys for the artifact role, 3) add a short-term bucket lifecycle to quarantine affected objects, 4) hotpatch runner to strip PII before upload.

ops-bot: Deployed S3 policy change at 03:12 UTC: `s3://redwood-eval-artifacts/staging/*` now denies `s3:GetObject` to `arn:aws:iam::public:*`. CI role keys rotated.

Sarah L.: Can we add a CI gating step that scans artifacts for common identifiers (email regex, customer_id pattern) and fails the job? Would greet having that as a merge-blocker for the fix.

Diego V.: Working on a PR now. Plan: add `artifact_sanitizer.py` with a function `sanitize_for_upload(obj)` that drops `customer_id`, `user_email`, `session_token` and replaces `example_id` with `sha256(example_id)`. Default flag `sanitize_artifacts=True` for CI runs. I'll add unit tests and a tiny e2e using 10 synthetic samples to assert no PII keys present post-upload.

Matt R.: Also add an INTEGRATION_TEST that runs the full harness with `--ci` and asserts `aws s3api head-object` metadata doesn't contain `x-amz-meta-customer`. Keep it fast (<30s).

Anya M.: Sarah — please coordinate with Customer Ops/Security for audit scope. We need to find all runs in last 30 days that used `runner>=2.3.0` and inventory objects. If any real customer IDs are present we need to 1) notify affected customers, 2) rotate any tokens.

Sarah L.: On it. Filing a security incident ticket and a slice for support notifications. Will run a quick grep/scan job across the bucket index.

eval-bot: CI job 1823456001 failed earlier: `unit-tests: artifact-sanitizer.test` — 3 failures.

Diego V.: Thanks eval-bot. Those were expected until I push the PR. Quick patch snippet I'm planning to land:

```python
# artifact_sanitizer.py
import hashlib
REDACT_KEYS = {"customer_id", "user_email", "session_token"}

def sanitize_for_upload(obj):
    sanitized = {}
    for k, v in obj.items():
        if k in REDACT_KEYS:
            continue
        if k == "example_id":
            hashed = hashlib.sha256(v.encode()).hexdigest()
            sanitized["example_id_sha256"] = hashed
        else:
            sanitized[k] = v
    return sanitized
```

Diego V.: Will also add a small audit script `tools/find_provenance_leaks.py` that searches objects for keys and heuristic PII.

Anya M.: Timeline: Diego quick PR w/ tests (1h), ops confirm all public access revoked and keys rotated (done), security audit + support notifications (Sarah, 3–6h). After PR lands, we'll run a job to reprocess staging artifacts to a quarantined prefix with sanitized copies, then delete originals.

Matt R.: One more ask: update the eval dashboard ingestion pipeline to stop reading `sample_provenance` fields. If we suddenly drop those keys ingestion could error. Put a compatibility shim to ignore unknown fields.

Sarah L.: Also check our logging/telemetry — we should not log full request bodies at INFO. Patch log level for `eval.runner.request` to DEBUG and scrub.

Diego V.: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/eval-harness/pull/489 — includes sanitizer, tests, and a new CI artifact-scan job. PTAL.

Anya M.: Great. After the PR merges, Diego please coordinate reprocessing job and deletion with ops; Sarah will handle customer comms. Marking this P0 until reprocessing is complete. :lock: :mag_right: :rotating_light:

Matt R.: Thx everyone. Small follow-up: we should add a lint rule that forbids dumping raw `request` objects to storage. I've got an ESLint-style rule for python AST we can adapt.

Diego V.: Adding that to the PR too.

Sarah L.: I'll update the incident ticket with owners and ETA.

Anya M.: Closing loop: we should add a config flag `retain_provenance` that is off by default in CI and on only for internal debugging builds behind a feature flag + restricted ACL.

Diego V.: Yep — feature-flagged and behind `can_read_provenance` IAM condition.

Matt R.: OK. We'll monitor for any other leaks. Good catch, Anya.

Anya M.: Thanks team. We'll sync in the 1pm standup if anything outstanding. :thumbsup:
